records.text: Candace Owens said SureFire Wireline's pump-down perforating work requires PETN explosive.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Okay. Surefire Wireline works with oil and gas companies and they specialize in what's known as pump down perforating for oil and gas wells. ... Okay, now why am I telling you that? Why do we need to know about that? Because that technique requires the use of a very specific explosive known as P-E-T-N.

verification.notes: Oil-well perforating uses shaped explosive charges, but PETN is not required. Manufacturer documentation identifies RDX- and HMX-based perforating charges, and technical sources list PETN, RDX, HMX, or HNS as alternatives. The categorical requires-PETN claim is directly contradicted.

records.text: I think Charlie Kirk's second redundant microphone was rigged as a shaped charge intended to hit his chest but accidentally hit his neck.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

And then I think they had to pivot, because the shaped charge accidentally—instead of hitting his chest and causing that .30-06 diameter, as would happen with PETN explosives, as we've demonstrated to you in the past—it accidentally, because of how Charlie (Charlie Kirk) was crouched... ... verification.notes: This is explicitly framed as a theory. Current charging records and 2026 hearing testimony allege a rooftop rifle shot and contain physical and video evidence supporting that allegation, while no forensic source supports a microphone shaped charge. records.text: PETN is the main component in military and commercial blasting caps, each of which contains less than one gram and can cause major damage.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #5 (Ep VMNWMXX1vO8)

appearances.snippet: It's the main component in military and commercial blasting caps. ... Each blasting cap has less than one gram of PETN and deals major damage.

verification.notes: Authoritative sources show standard detonators commonly use PETN as the secondary or output charge and give representative charges of about 0.45 to 0.60 grams, below one gram. But blasting-cap designs vary, including military caps using RDX or PETN, so the universal military-and-commercial wording and generalized damage claim are too broad.

sources.title: United Nations standard detonator specifications
sources.relevance: Specifies a standard detonator secondary PETN charge of 0.60 grams.

sources.title: National Academies report on detonators
sources.relevance: Explains that detonator output charge is typically PETN while the priming charge can use other compounds.
